evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.23.4: eā ipsā hōrā (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 3.21: trīgintā diēs erant ipsī, it was just thirty days (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin puts the “just” on the word it marks: id ipsum, just that; tum ipsum, just then; nunc ipsum, right now, at this very moment (Cic. Att. 7.3.2, Lewis & Short); with numbers, exactly.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.142: haec cum maximē loquerētur, just as he was saying this (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 87: just as, cum maximē; just then, tunc maximē
terms.comment: nunc cum maximē, right now, at this very time (Cic. Sen. 38, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē
phrases.english: there my little Tullia was waiting for me, on her very birthday

phrases.latin: Salvum tē advenīre, Dēmea, gaudēmus. — Ehem, opportūnē: tē ipsum quaeritō.
phrases.english: We’re glad to see you safely here, Demea. — Ah, good timing: you’re just the man I’m looking for.

phrases.latin: ōlim mihi nūllās epistulās mittis. nihil est, inquis, quod scrībam. at hoc ipsum scrībe, nihil esse quod scrībās
phrases.english: you haven’t sent me a letter for ages. ‘There’s nothing to write,’ you say. Then write just that: that there’s nothing to write
